detailedExplanation: Verified against The Tiffin Girls’ School Year 9 Chemistry Curriculum Outline 2026–27 (AQA GCSE Chemistry 8462).
Alkenes contain a carbon–carbon double bond. In an addition reaction, the double bond opens and atoms are added across the two carbon atoms.
Hydrogenation adds hydrogen to form an alkane. Hydration adds steam to form an alcohol. Halogenation adds a halogen such as bromine to form a dihalogeno product.
Bromine water can be used as a test for unsaturation: an alkene decolourises the orange/brown bromine-water solution.

additionalSourceSections.heading: Core Idea
additionalSourceSections.body:
Alkene C=C opens during addition:
+ H₂ → alkane (hydrogenation)
+ H₂O/steam → alcohol (hydration)
+ halogen, e.g. Br₂ → dihalogeno compound
Bromine water is decolourised by an alkene.
